The safety of intravenous fluorescein for confocal laser endomicroscopy in the gastrointestinal tract. BACKGROUND Confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) is rapidly emerging as a valuable tool for gastrointestinal endoscopic imaging. Fluorescent contrast agents are used to optimize imaging with CLE, and intravenous fluorescein is the most widely used contrast agent. Fluorescein is FDA-cleared for diagnostic angiography of the retina. For these indications, the safety profile of fluorescein has been well-documented; however, to date, fluorescein is not cleared for use with CLE. AIMS To estimate the rate of serious and total adverse events attributable to intravenous fluorescein when used for gastrointestinal CLE.
